clue.text: New record releases with something for the Scottish market

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so the following word's letter is let out of the build

blocks.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A record label puts out new singles aimed specially at buyers in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: With is the letter released from the first word. A neep is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, eaten with haggis on Burns Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a turnip is a vegetable sold in Scottish markets, so it is something for that market.

clue.text: Fragmented story going on at length about lives upset party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the long story goes around the middle pieces
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for party is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: an epic is a long narrative
lives in the sense exists, is
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A disjointed tale rambles on about the lives of guests at a party that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Lives is the verb (exists), not the plural noun, and story going on at length is one long block, not three.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic happens in separate, irregular bursts, so it is broken into fragments rather than continuous.

clue.text: Ban selection of executive toys

indicators.note: a selection is only some of what is there, so the letters are picked out from inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to prohibit some of the desk gadgets beloved of managers.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an official prohibition or refusal, just as a ban forbids something.

clue.text: Removes bodies from very easy test

indicators.note: a body is the trunk without head or limbs, so each word loses its first and last letters and keeps its centre

blocks.note: the inside of very
the inside of easy
the inside of test

explanation.surface: Something that strips away corpses in a very simple examination, a slightly macabre exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Bodies is also a Sex Pistols song, one of several of their titles worked into this puzzle's clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, which is the same as taking something away completely.

clue.text: Submission originally reprinted inaccurate condition of stock

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept
something inaccurate is not set out correctly, so these letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor complains that a submitted piece came back reprinted wrongly, in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here means livestock, not shares or goods; rinderpest is a cattle plague. Submission is also a Sex Pistols song.
explanation.definitionFit: Rinderpest is an infectious viral disease of cattle, so it is an illness afflicting farm animals.

clue.text: Retro album cover for Travis is high point

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the whole build is read from right to left
a cover wraps the outside, so only the outermost letters of the band's name are kept

blocks.note: an LP, spelt out as a word
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A retro-style sleeve for a Travis album is the band's finest moment; Travis are a Scottish rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: Album must be spelt out as a word, not left as its two-letter abbreviation, for the reversal to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall spire of a church, often the highest point of a town's skyline.

clue.text: Band material influenced broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word for influenced is to be heard rather than seen

blocks.note: first meaning: the British indie group of the 1990s
second meaning: soft leather with a napped finish
influenced is swayed, which is said the same way

explanation.surface: The fabric a group wears was chosen under the sway of television.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: Suede the Britpop band, suede the leather, and swayed said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a leather with a brushed surface used for clothing, and also the name of a London rock group.

clue.text: Rotten liar's rants

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so the following letters break up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Johnny Rotten, the Sex Pistols singer, delivers a liar's tirade; Liar is also one of their songs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly and loudly, so it means the same as rants as a verb.

clue.text: Have problems repeating oneself to begin with

blocks.note: first meaning: to struggle with speech, falter
second meaning: saying the opening sounds of words over and over

explanation.surface: Someone struggles because they keep going over the same ground from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Repeating oneself suggests a bore, but it is the involuntary repetition of initial sounds. Problems is also a Sex Pistols song.
explanation.definitionFit: To stammer is to speak haltingly with involuntary pauses and repeated first sounds, a speech impediment.

clue.text: They appeared on boundary-defining album

blocks.note: surface reading: a book of maps showing frontiers
setter's reading: the group whose 1977 album title runs round this grid's perimeter, defining its boundary

explanation.surface: Some people featured in an atlas of national borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading clockwise round the grid's edge, the unchecked letters spell NEVER MIND THE BOLLOCKS, the album that defines the puzzle's boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The British punk group fronted by Johnny Rotten made Never Mind the Bollocks, the record spelt round the border.

clue.text: Drink and drive in the morning

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names
am stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A warning against having a drink and then getting behind the wheel the next morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small measure of whisky or other spirits, a drink in Scotland especially.

clue.text: Moaned about study that scared me

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so everything that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: a den is a private study
the cry someone gives when frightened

explanation.surface: Someone groaned about a piece of research that frightened them.
explanation.walkthrough: DEN plus EEK, all reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief for the dead, so keened means lamented or moaned aloud.

clue.text: I refuse to flush as toilet's completely blocked

indicators.note: to flush is to stir up and send scattering, as with game birds, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the word you say to refuse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declines to pull the chain because the lavatory is totally clogged.
explanation.walkthrough: The toilet and flush are a plumbing scene, but the definition is about traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic that is bumper to bumper, each vehicle's front against the one ahead's rear, is jammed and cannot move.

clue.text: Fresh pitas filled with butter and meat

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
something filled has another thing put inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A sandwich order: new flatbreads spread with butter and filled with meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter looks like the dairy spread, but it is one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a seasoned smoked beef, a cured cold meat often served in sandwiches.

clue.text: Press release initially upset EMI chief

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is kept
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the record label's name reads from the bottom

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement to journalists annoyed the boss of the record company EMI.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI famously dropped the Sex Pistols in 1977, and EMI is also one of their songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime as an adjective means first in importance, the same sense as chief in phrases like main concern.

clue.text: Obstinate person taking courses at regular intervals

indicators.note: regular intervals mean evenly spaced picks, so every second letter of the word is used

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A stubborn student signs up for classes now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuss is an informal word for a person, typically an awkward or contrary one, as in an obstinate old cuss.

clue.text: Bringing up Australian native stealing clothing causes offence

indicators.note: a thief takes something and holds it, so the bird's name keeps the clothing inside
in a down clue, bringing up means lifting from the bottom, so the result reads upwards

blocks.note: the emu is a flightless bird native to Australia
garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Raising the matter of an Aboriginal person accused of theft of clothes gives offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Australian native looks like a person, but crosswords often mean the flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to feel resentment or take offence at a slight.

clue.text: Reduce speed following double bluff

indicators.note: to reduce something is to make it shorter, so the word for speed loses its final letter
double means two of the same, so the abbreviation is written twice

blocks.note: as in going at a fast clip
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 10f; doubled

explanation.surface: Advice to a card player: slow down after attempting a double bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: Double bluff reads as a poker ploy; bluff alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep headland or bank, which is a cliff by another name.

clue.text: Dire outcome of participation having no consequences?

definitions.text: Dire outcome of participation having no consequences?

blocks.note: setter's reading: taking part and getting the benefit without paying, a ride with nothing owed
setter's reading in reverse: the answer read as wordplay, its second word set loose, produces dire

explanation.surface: A grim warning that joining in without any repercussions ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat the first word of the answer as an anagram signal and its second word as letters, and they come out as Dire.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting something for nothing, enjoying benefits of a group without contributing, means taking part with no cost to oneself.

clue.text: Win is one way to retain The Ashes reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the word is to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.clueFragment: one way to retain The Ashes
blocks.note: the Ashes cricket trophy is a tiny urn, and an urn holds ashes

explanation.surface: A sports commentator says victory is one way England can keep hold of the Ashes, the England–Australia cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a funeral urn literally retains ashes. The match only holds in non-rhotic accents.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain something through effort, as in to win a reward or wage.

clue.text: Let drunk close tab

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the following letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bar staff are told to let a tipsy customer settle their bill and finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Let looks like allow, but here it is the noun in 'without let or hindrance', an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Let as an old noun means a hindrance or impediment, which is exactly a thing in the way.

clue.text: Small business satisfied with round figure for total

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
as in met demands
the circular numeral zero

explanation.surface: A small firm is happy to round its accounts up to a neat sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To total as a verb is to add up to an amount, and come to is the everyday phrasal verb for that.

clue.text: Reach conclusion after reading everything but the introduction

indicators.note: all except the start means the opening letter is dropped
after means placed behind, so the word for conclusion comes second

blocks.note: text is reading matter
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A reader comes to a verdict having skipped the opening chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to stretch out to a point, so it has the sense of to reach as far as.

clue.text: Vicious American disembowelled sweetheart in New York

indicators.note: with the innards taken out, only the outer letters of the following word remain
in places these pieces inside the abbreviation for the city

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
the first and last letters
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A grisly crime story: a cruel American gutted his girlfriend in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: Disembowelled applies to sweetheart, not American. New York is also a Sex Pistols song.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and vicious both describe someone spiteful and cruel who wishes to cause harm.

clue.text: Most unsuitable model for Oxford's Assembly?

blocks.note: first meaning: the least likely or appropriate
second meaning: a cobbler's foot-shaped form on which a shoe such as an Oxford is built

explanation.surface: A poor choice of role model for the university's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's Assembly suggests a university body, but an Oxford is a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's form shaped like a foot is the pattern a shoe is assembled on; last also means least suitable.

clue.text: Unbridled anarchy disturbs drippy Queen fan perhaps

indicators.note: without a bridle the horse loses its head harness; here the word loses both ends and keeps the middle
to disturb is to break into, so these letters burst into the middle of the next word

blocks.note: drippy means moist
the inside of the word

explanation.surface: Wild chaos upsets a soppy royalist, nodding to the Sex Pistols' Anarchy in the UK and God Save the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: NARCH breaks into MOIST. Queen fan looks like a fan of the rock band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of rule by a king or queen admires the crown, so one example is a devotee of the Queen.

clue.text: No expression of doubt in song having no feelings

indicators.note: no means without, so the sound of doubt is taken away

blocks.note: a number is a song in a show or set
the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: A singer plainly sure of a heartfelt ballad that leaves listeners cold; No Feelings is a Sex Pistols song.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without sensation, whether physically or emotionally, is being deadened to sensation.

clue.text: Chop up small offcut from hardwood tree

indicators.note: a small offcut is just a sliver from the start of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A carpenter is told to cut a scrap of timber off a hardwood tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Ash is itself a hardwood, which makes the surface seamless.
explanation.definitionFit: To hash food is to cut it into small pieces, as in hash browns or corned beef hash.

clue.text: Final three of seventeen return court order

indicators.note: the final three are the last three letters of the answer referred to
to return is to go back, so those letters run the other way

blocks.note: seventeen means the answer at 17 down, whose last three letters these are
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: The last three of seventeen defendants come back for a judge's ruling; Seventeen is a Sex Pistols song.
explanation.walkthrough: Seventeen is a cross-reference to 17 down, FREE RIDE; its last three letters are turned round to give EDI.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or proclamation issued by an authority, a command or order.

clue.text: Decency of every other character in smutty song's lines

indicators.note: every other means alternate, so only the second, fourth and sixth letters are kept
to line something is to cover its inside, so the kept letters form a lining around the next piece

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
an ode is a lyric poem meant to be sung, plus the S

explanation.surface: Propriety is put to the test by a filthy song's lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines looks like lyrics, but it is a verb: the kept letters line the songs, wrapping round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is propriety in dress and behaviour, avoiding indecency, so it is a synonym of decency.
